data.narrative:
Steady Energy is a Series G climate and energy technology company founded by Tommi Nyman, Hannes Haapalahti, and Petteri Tenhunen, having raised €32M to date. The relevant comp universe comprises nine private frontier-tech peers in Climate & Energy alongside one public comparable (LNZA), though this narrow set presents material constraints for valuation triangulation.

Standard methodologies prove inapplicable here. Stage-progression analysis, while theoretically suited to Series G positioning, cannot be executed reliably: the implied $2.2B valuation resulting from a $1.75B base value and 1.25x multiplier exceeds 20x the company's total capital raised, suggesting the funding-proxy input is unreliable. Peer-median methodology similarly cannot proceed: while nine same-sector companies exist in the comp universe, filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage transactions with comparable valuation tiers yields fewer than three datapoints—the minimum threshold for meaningful median derivation. Broadening filters to all-sector peers would introduce material sector basis risk.

No triangulated valuation range can be responsibly derived from the available data. A credible analysis would require either (1) executable transaction or revenue multiples from a sufficiently sized peer subset at similar maturity, (2) contemporaneous financing round data for Steady Energy, or (3) operational metrics enabling revenue or cash-flow multiple application. The primary uncertainty remains the absence of narrow peer comparables at Series G maturity within frontier climate tech.
